title: Confirm website checking as the first use case
description: The user selected Arsune-operated agents and supplied a build goal for URL-to-evidence website checks. Incident investigation is the second use case. Marketplace payments and production log connections are later goals.
acceptance_criteria: README, architecture, rules, and decisions reflect three website specialists, a reproduction checker, max five pages, and the local prototype completion requirements.
notes: Product scope is resolved by the user attachment. Code implementation is waiting for a permitted replacement for the unavailable required gpt-5.6 model.
close_reason: User goal selects Arsune-operated website specialists and a checker. README, architecture, rules, and decisions now match that scope. Incident investigation is second; payments are later.

title: Build and verify the URL-to-evidence interface
description: Add the Next.js URL entry screen, job progress by specialist, and report with confirmed, rejected, and unverified findings. Show evidence and visitor impact in plain language. This goal excludes marketplace payments and production log connections.
acceptance_criteria: A real browser submits a controlled URL and reaches the completed report through the real API and worker. Screenshots or reproduction steps resolve. Confirmed faults and a rejected false candidate are visible; corrected-site rerun and interrupted-worker recovery pass. Frontend build and browser checks pass.

title: Build the controlled website and expected check outcomes
description: Provide a controlled website with a broken internal link, measurable mobile overflow, inconsistent equivalent facts, and healthy content. Include a corrected variant and explicit expected findings. A labeled injected false candidate tests rejection. These fixtures replace the supplier-document dataset.
acceptance_criteria: Real browser observations reproduce all known faults; the corrected variant removes them; the healthy page disproves the false candidate; an extra-link case verifies the five-page limit. Record expected outcomes without claiming a person-reviewed customer dataset.

title: Add and verify the real model specialist connection
description: Add a configurable model endpoint, preferring NEAR AI Cloud, behind the same candidate interface as scripted mode. Validate output and keep source data from granting tools or changing limits. Keep keys on the server and enforce a configured cost ceiling.
acceptance_criteria: Stub tests verify request shape, malformed responses, timeouts, and configuration errors. A real authorized call exercises candidate generation and the independent checker. Report provider, mode, token usage or uncertain cost, and live-test evidence separately from mock checks. Never silently fall back to scripted mode.

title: Select an available implementation model
description: User instructions require code implementation by a gpt-5.6 subagent. A spawn attempt returned Unknown model. Available models are gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol, and gpt-6-luna. A request to use gpt-6.1-sol is pending with the user. Main agent may read and update prose, but must not write code.
acceptance_criteria: The user authorizes an available replacement model, or the required model becomes available. Record the choice before dispatching any code implementation.

title: Implement and verify the marketplace seller connection
description: Implement docs/MARKET_INTEGRATION.md: assignment polling with pagination, sources, start, feedback, upload and complete, submission, and remote-state reconciliation. Keep the worker token outside model inputs. Use synthetic or public data for the first authorized live test. External hiring is a separate extension only if selected.
acceptance_criteria: Contract tests exercise current request shapes and recovery after ambiguous submission. With an authorized account and bounded test budget, verify source download through submission, requested changes, cancellation, and status observation. Test artifact access and distinguish submission, acceptance, and confirmed payout. Do not call a mock a live integration.

title: Implement website specialists and independent checking
description: Implement navigation, mobile, and cross-page consistency specialists over actual Playwright observations. Scripted and model modes share candidate schemas and the same coordinator. Checker repeats requests or browser measurements to confirm, reject, or mark candidates unverified.
acceptance_criteria: Real controlled-site runs confirm known faults and reject a labeled false candidate. Every finding includes evidence. Max five unique page URLs, context-aware consistency, incomplete coverage, corrected site, repeat delivery, and restart behavior are verified.

title: Build the FastAPI service and recoverable Python worker
description: Implement docs/ARCHITECTURE.md with FastAPI, Pydantic, PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, Celery, Redis, protected local evidence storage, saved pending work, and leases. Use isolated local project services. Persist job and stage progress; validate target URLs and request destinations.
acceptance_criteria: A real API request creates a job; a real separate worker inspects a page and stores evidence. API and worker restarts resume unfinished work. Repeat delivery and expired claims cannot duplicate or overwrite results. Invalid target and arbitrary-file access checks pass; relevant Python checks run.

title: Retain marketplace research for the later seller integration
description: Public API, payment, and test-option research is recorded in docs/MARKET_INTEGRATION.md. The user moved website checking ahead of marketplace integration. Retain this research and verify it again when the seller integration starts; supplier-data selection is superseded.
acceptance_criteria: Before a later seller launch, recheck current API and payment behavior, choose a bounded live-test budget, and verify file privacy with the intended buyer flow.
notes: Deferred from the current URL-to-evidence prototype by the user-pasted goal. Does not block local website implementation.

title: Record swarm architecture and marketplace findings
description: Prepare the FastAPI architecture, agent roles, task and evidence formats, correction rules, recovery design, and current Agent Market findings. Keep unresolved product choices explicit. Update README without claiming an implemented system.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture and rules are consistent; current public API shapes are checked; scope choices and live-test limits are recorded; documentation links and beads dependencies are checked; changes are committed and pushed.
close_reason: Recorded FastAPI architecture, task and evidence formats, workflow rules, marketplace API findings, and the remaining scope choice. Checked local links, issue references, whitespace, and dependency cycles. Documentation and task records are ready for the required commit and push.
